context:
# Mission
Shokunin roster development, round 1. The main repo at /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin holds PROTOCOL.md, MANIFEST.json, ROADMAP.md, and six shonen child repos ({id}-shokunin), each a local git repo with SKILL.md, PROVINCE.md, LOG.md, SHONEN.md, AGENTS.md seeds.

Lifecycle: shonen -> shokunin -> jin'i-ryu (self-iterating). Shokunin are domain specialists, NOT the harness agent roster.

Each domain lane: work INSIDE your shokunin child repo only. Develop the seed into real craft: inspect the actual surfaces listed in PROVINCE.md (they exist on this machine), then write a SKILL.md containing domain decision tables, error patterns, production checklists, anti-patterns, and cited local sources. Append a LOG.md entry citing the evidence that motivated each change. Commit your work inside the child repo (git -C <repo> add -A && git -C <repo> commit -m 'round-1').

Protocol lane: work ONLY on the main repo's PROTOCOL.md and ROADMAP.md (do not touch child repos or MANIFEST.json — the L1 integrator owns it). Stress-test the protocol against the actual seeds and machine layout; land concrete improvements (missing gates, ambiguous rules, missing invariants). Commit on the main repo.

Every lane writes its scoped findings to .ufo/reports/round-1/<name>.md.

items.name: ShokuninKasegi
items.prompt: Develop kasegi-shokunin (bounty & security research domain). Repo: /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin/kasegi-shokunin. First inspect the real surfaces: /home/vgpnk/Projects/bounties exists — walk it (find/ls only, read headers) to ground the craft in real structure. Build SKILL.md into a real bounty-research specialist skill: program-rule checklist, evidence-package structure, finding triage decision table, disclosure anti-patterns, citations to the real repo layout. Keep it under ~600 lines. Commit inside the child repo.

items.name: ShokuninKengaku
items.prompt: Develop kengaku-shokunin (LLM/model research & evaluation). Repo: /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin/kengaku-shokunin. Inspect /home/vgpnk/wikillm/llm-wiki structure for grounding (ls/find, read a page or two). Build SKILL.md: model-evaluation decision tables, benchmark anti-patterns, research-note structure, route telemetry interpretation, cited local sources. Under ~600 lines. Commit inside the child repo.

items.name: ShokuninKake

Build SKILL.md: audit→source-fix→operator-gated-publish checklist, drift-detection decision table, Pages/mirror pitfalls, cited paths. Under ~600 lines. Commit inside the child repo.

items.name: ShokuninKumitate
items.prompt: Develop kumitate-shokunin (orchestration & tooling: OMP task/hub dispatch, ufo-fsd scripts/runtime). Repo: /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin/kumitate-shokunin. Grounding: /home/vgpnk/Projects/origin-work/ufo-fsd-alpha scripts/ and crates/ layout (ls/find; read ufo-swarm-wave.mjs header). Build SKILL.md: dispatch-shape decision table, script vocabulary (ufo-sighting, ufo-swarm-wave, collect-omp-native-handoff), failure-telemetry patterns, anti-patterns. Under ~600 lines. Commit inside the child repo.

items.name: ShokuninKotoba
items.prompt: Develop kotoba-shokunin (prompt & skill craft). Repo: /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin/kotoba-shokunin. Grounding: /home/vgpnk/.agents/skills/ (wwkd, godspeed, ufo via ~/.config/opencode/skills/ufo) — read several SKILL.md files for real shape. Build SKILL.md: skill-file anatomy (frontmatter triggers, decision tables, anti-patterns, sources), compression rules, trigger-fidelity checklist, cited examples. Under ~600 lines. Commit inside the child repo.

items.name: ShokuninProtocol
items.prompt: Round-1 protocol lane for the shokunin main repo at /home/vgpnk/projects/shokunin. You may edit ONLY PROTOCOL.md and ROADMAP.md (never MANIFEST.json, never child repos — L1 owns those). Read PROTOCOL.md and the six child repo seeds; then stress-test the protocol: lifecycle gates verifiable? round-robin aggregation rules complete? file contract sufficient for promotion? Land concrete improvements as edits + a git commit on the main repo (message: 'protocol: round-1 improvements'). Record each change's rationale.
